summary: A September 2008 HR Bartender blog post by Sharlyn Lauby uses an episode of the TV show Scrubs to argue that workplaces should embrace the pursuit of perfection rather than treat it as a flaw. Dr. Cox's line about the endless pursuit of perfection, from an episode about 'the perfect game,' becomes the model. The author argues that striving for perfection and falling short is better than aiming low, because it pushes people to improve.
one_line: Sharlyn Lauby argues, using a Scrubs episode and Dr. Cox, that workplaces should embrace striving for perfection as a driver of improvement.
key_facts: The post was published on September 4, 2008 on the HR Bartender blog.
The author describes Dr. Cox as their favorite character on the television show Scrubs.
Dr. Cox is played by John C. McGinley, according to the post.
In the episode about 'the perfect game,' Dr. Cox works with other doctors to keep everyone in the hospital alive for 24 hours.
In the episode, a patient dies in the final minutes, and another doctor suggests they can wait to report the time of death because only they know.
Dr. Cox responds: 'It's not about winning under false pretenses. It's about the endless pursuit of perfection.'
The post says that in workplaces, perfection is often viewed as a bad thing.
The post notes that job applicants often name 'they are a perfectionist' as their weakness.
The author asks whether, if we strive for perfection and fall short, that is better than shooting for less and hitting it.
The author concludes that aiming for perfection pushes us to improve and to be the absolute best we can be.
A reader comment from RMSmithJr, dated December 9, 2012, says they choose the 'Pursuit of Excellence' in all they do.
Sharlyn Lauby is described as an HR pro turned consultant who created HR Bartender.
